Quick reference · 0001

Process environments

Bash and Zsh commands for controlling what a child process receives.

IntentCommandScope
Shell variableKEY=valueCurrent shell only
Export nowexport KEY=valueCurrent shell and future children
Export existingexport KEYFuture children receive current value
One commandKEY=value commandThat command and its children
Remove valueunset KEYCurrent shell and future children
Inspect exported valuesenv or export -pCurrent process environment
Inspect from Bunbun -e 'console.log(process.env.KEY)'What Bun actually received
Debugging question: which process loaded or exported the value, and was the target process started afterward as its child?

Loading a trusted, shell-compatible file

set -a          # automatically export assignments
. ./.env       # `source .env` also works in Bash/Zsh
set +a          # turn automatic export back off

set -a is defined by the Bash manual. Sourcing executes the file as shell code; do it only with trusted, shell-compatible content. A dotenv parser and a shell are not guaranteed to accept identical syntax.

Precedence principle

“Which value wins?” has no universal answer. Precedence belongs to the loader—Bun, Wrangler, Docker Compose, or another tool. Consult that tool's documented order.
